setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 13): net income $15.3B, EPS $5.57, ROTCE 20%, revenue $50.9B (+8% YoY), expense $27.3B (+12%), credit costs $2.7B (net charge-offs $2.2B, reserve build $539M), including $658M of net investment securities losses in Corporate. Secondary coverage dated Oct 31 calls this the first EPS miss since 2023, against a consensus of roughly $5.90.

Consensus for fiscal Q4 2026 (report due 2027-01-14 after the close) is EPS $5.92 and revenue $51.79B. The correct year-ago base is Q4 2025, with revenue of $45.80B and diluted EPS of $4.63. That makes consensus about +13.1% on revenue and +27.9% on EPS. The fact sheet's derived growth (+11.5% revenue, +16.8% EPS) divides by Q3 2025 ($46.43B, $5.07), which is the wrong quarter. Both are shown. For the same fiscal-quarter comparison, the Q4 2025 base is the right one.

The Q4 2025 EPS base is depressed. Its provision was $4,655M including $2.2B tied to the Apple Card transaction, and net income was $13,025M. Adding back about $2.2B pre-tax at an assumed ~25% tax rate over about 2.74B diluted shares lifts the base by roughly $0.60, to about $5.23. Consensus EPS growth on that adjusted base is then roughly +13%, not +28%. This is my approximation, not a sourced figure.

Q3 call guidance: Q4 NII ex-Markets about $25.5B, total NII about $28B, expense about $27.5B and card NCO about 3.2% for the full year. A first 2027 central case for NII ex-Markets is about $107B. Management said it was updating full-year guidance by giving the fourth quarter, so Q4 is largely a test against these figures.

Consensus revenue implies roughly flat noninterest revenue quarter on quarter. Q3 noninterest revenue was about $23.8B (revenue $50.9B less NII $27.1B), and Q4 consensus revenue of $51.79B less guided NII of about $28B is also about $23.8B. That is only +1.7% revenue growth from Q3. It leaves room for a normal Markets seasonal decline and a late-September IB slowdown to be offset by the non-recurrence of Q3's $658M securities losses. This is derived arithmetic.

Capital: standardized CET1 fell to 13.9% from 14.2% in Q2 (a 30bp decline on higher RWA, OCI losses and distributions). Secondary coverage says net buybacks fell to $664M from $6.2B a year ago, and an analyst on the call cited a roughly $1B buyback. The Q2 10-Q shows gross repurchases of $6.7B. A new $50B authorization began July 1 and the dividend was raised to $1.65.

Stock setup: price $337.04 against a consensus price target of $373.36 (+10.8%). Post-call rating actions were all 'maintained' (Citi Neutral, Truist Hold, Baird Neutral, Morgan Stanley Equal Weight, RBC Outperform, Barclays Overweight; UBS Buy on Oct 5). Average closing move around reports has been ±2.1% over the last 8, with 3 beats and 1 miss in the last 4 quarters (average surprise +2.2%). view.text: Illustrative bridge, not a sourced analyst assumption: revenue $51.79B less guided expense of about $27.5B and an assumed provision of about $2.7B gives pre-tax income of about $21.6B. At a 24-25% tax rate, after preferred dividends and participating securities, on roughly 2.65-2.69B shares, that is about $5.9. So $5.92 is arithmetically consistent with the guides. Rough sensitivities: 1pt of tax rate is about $0.08, $0.5B of provision about $0.14, and 1% of share count about $0.06. Q3's implied tax rate (about 27% on rounded call figures) was above the H1 rate of 21.6%.

since_filing.text: The Q3 print on Oct 13 updated the July outlook (NII $105.5B, ex-Markets $96.5B, adjusted expense $107.5B, card NCO ~3.2%). Q4 NII and expense were given, and a 2027 NII central case was added. The Q3 10-Q has not yet been filed or read, so Q3 repurchase dollars, AOCI, tax and legal detail are unverified.

Q3 results versus the 10-Q period: EPS $5.57 (Q2: $7.70, which included the $4.6B Visa gain), expense $27.3B, credit costs $2.7B with a $539M reserve build (Q2 build: $149M), CET1 13.9% (Q2: 14.2%), standardized RWA up about $52B. The CFO attributed the CET1 decline to OCI losses, higher RWA and capital distributions, and did not quantify OCI.

Capital return changed sharply. Gross buybacks were $6.7B in Q2. An analyst framed Q3 as a $1B buyback against a normal cadence of about $7B, and TIKR (Oct 31) reports net buybacks of $664M versus $6.2B. Management did not state a Q3 figure in the transcript text read and did not dispute the framing. Note the definition gap: the Q2 10-Q shows gross repurchases of $6,703M and only $51M of reissuance, so a 'net $6.2B' base does not tie simply to Q2. The figures are unreconciled until the Q3 10-Q.
On Oct 20 JPM closed senior note offerings totaling about $7.0B (derived: $350M floating-rate notes due 2030, $2.9B fixed-to-floating notes due 2030, $3.75B fixed-to-floating notes due 2037).

Rates backdrop: the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (10-2 vote). As of Oct 30 the 10-year yield 'recently fell from 24-year highs'. The '6% 10-year' on the call was an analyst hypothetical, and Dimon said 'we're not predicting it'. BAC's 10-Q (filed Oct 30) shows 9/30 spot rates of fed funds 4.00% and 10-year 4.90%, with a 12-month forward fed funds of 5.00%.

Regulatory and legal: the OCC released a report of its supervisory review of debanking activities at the nine largest national banks it supervises, including JPMorgan Chase Bank. A weekly summary dated Oct 25 says neither the OCC nor CFPB document sets a compliance date, that the OCC didn't quantify how many accounts were affected, and that JPM is contesting the Trump debanking suit in a new venue. No JPM-specific penalty or settlement was found.

Peer reads: Citi Q3 IB revenue +9% to $1.35B (equity capital markets +77%, advisory -4%) and Goldman record advisory of $1.65B (+18%). Capital One's Q3 domestic card charge-off rate was 3.98%, down 65bp YoY. BAC's Q3 provision fell YoY, with its allowance down on card and CRE improvement, partly offset by a qualitative Middle East reserve. Morningstar's read of Q3 bank earnings: a September Fed hike, higher long-end rates and energy prices slowed deals and FICC volumes, while consumer spending and credit quality held up.

Sell-side reaction since Q3: all rating actions in the data were 'maintained' (Oct 14-15), the consensus price target is $373.36 against a price of $337.04, and the stock was reported 8.4% below its 52-week high on Oct 27.

key_debates.question: Does Q4 revenue reach consensus ($51.79B) if IB slowed in late September and Markets follows normal seasonality?

bull.text: Dimon expects a smaller-than-normal seasonal Markets decline, the IB pipeline is described as robust, and Equities (prime and derivatives, +49% in Q3) keeps outperforming. Q3's $658M securities losses need not recur, and consensus needs only +1.7% over Q3.

bear.text: The CFO's base case is a normal Q3-to-Q4 Markets decline. IB activity slowed in the second half of September amid the rate sell-off, and Dimon said the pipeline is 'like an accordion' that can open and close quickly. Fixed Income was -4% in Q3. Consensus revenue of $51.79B is only about 1.7% above Q3's $50.9B despite these headwinds.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Markets and IB revenue lines, the extent of seasonal decline, and any further Corporate securities losses in the Jan 14 report.

key_debates.question: Is the sharply lower buyback pace a smart redeployment or a drag on EPS and capital returns?

bull.text: Management argues organic deployment (lending, the Security and Resiliency Initiative, other growth initiatives) earns better returns than repurchasing stock at a roughly 6% earnings yield. About $30B of excess capital is estimated, and the new $50B authorization began July 1.

bear.text: CET1 has already fallen from about 15.7% to 13.9%. The RWA increase of about $52B in Q3 and the 6% (about 4% combined) re-proposal impact on required CET1 limit flexibility. A smaller buyback also reduces the share-count lift to EPS and TBVPS. Management did not give a Q4 pace.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 share count and repurchase dollars, the Q3 10-Q repurchase table, and final Basel III/GSIB rules expected around year-end.

key_debates.question: Is the $107B 2027 NII ex-Markets case credible in a rising-rate setting?

bull.text: JPM remains asset-sensitive, with deposit betas lower than modeled. About half of the $5B growth is curve and hikes, and the rest is continued balance-sheet and mix trends. Net new checking accounts of about 650K and consumer deposit growth of 4% YoY support the base.

bear.text: The CFO flagged possible migration into CDs and premium deposits and slightly weaker deposit growth as rates rise, called this cycle unprecedented for beta modeling, and noted wholesale deposit growth is likely weaker than this year. BAC says higher short-end rates raise deposit pricing faster and reduce asset sensitivity. The central case is highly uncertain.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 NII ex-Markets versus $25.5B, deposit mix and CCB deposit margin disclosure, and the refinement of the 2027 case on the Q4 call.

key_debates.question: Is credit stable enough that Q4 provision stays near $2.7B?

bull.text: Management called corporate credit stable and the Q3 wholesale build was driven by new activity, not downgrades. The consumer is described as very healthy on a strong labor market, and H1 card NCOs of 3.40% against a guide of about 3.2% leave room. Peer card losses (Capital One 3.98%, -65bp YoY) are improving.

bear.text: Management said pressures are building: higher rates, energy and fuel costs. An extended hiking cycle would mean higher unemployment and weaker card credit. At Q2, criticized wholesale exposure rose to $50.3B, with Consumer & Retail up $1.3B. Management is tightening credit terms, citing loose covenants and priming.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 net charge-offs, the reserve build, and card delinquency and wholesale criticized disclosures in the Q3 10-Q and the Q4 release.

description.text: Revenue beats $51.79B on a smaller-than-normal Markets seasonal decline and resilient advisory, with no repeat of Q3's $658M securities losses. A provision at or below $2.7B and a tax rate nearer the H1 level of 21.6% push EPS above $5.92, partly offsetting a muted buyback.

description.text: Results land near consensus ($51.79B revenue, $5.92 EPS). NII ex-Markets is about $25.5B, total NII about $28B, expense about $27.5B and a provision near Q3's $2.7B. Buybacks stay subdued, and the 2027 NII case is reiterated or modestly refined.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: The IB slowdown that began in late September carries into Q4 and Markets declines normally, so revenue misses despite guided NII. Expense stays near $27.5B on volume-related costs and the provision rises on rates and energy pressure. A second quarter of securities losses or a higher tax rate would widen the gap to $5.92, as in Q3's miss.

triggers: IB fees fall short; advisory completions slow as rates rise
Markets revenue declines more than seasonally
Reserve build or net charge-offs above Q3; wholesale downgrades in Consumer & Retail or Industrials
Tax rate similar to Q3's implied ~27%
Deposit mix shifts to CDs and pressures NII ex-Markets below $25.5B

claim.text: Revenue risk concentrated in Markets and IB: IB activity slowed in late September, the Q4 Markets seasonal decline is uncertain (CFO base case normal, CEO expects less), and consensus revenue of $51.79B only needs about +1.7% over Q3's $50.9B.

Credit costs and reserve builds: the Q3 build of $539M was wholesale-driven. Management cites pressures from rates, energy and fuel prices, and said an extended hiking cycle would mean higher unemployment and weaker card credit. Morningstar notes a September Fed hike and higher energy prices.

Securities repositioning losses in Treasury and CIO: Q3 had $658M of net investment securities losses (about 18c per share), and the 10-Q describes repositioning sales of GSE and agency MBS. No Q4 guidance on further losses was found.

Capital and rules: CET1 fell to 13.9% on RWA growth, OCI and distributions. The Basel III re-proposal would raise required CET1 by about 6% (about 4% combined with the GSIB proposal). Final rules are expected around year-end according to an analyst on the call, and buyback pace is unguided.

Deposit and NII risk in a rising-rate cycle: possible migration from checking and savings into CDs and higher-beta products, wholesale deposits that are more competitive, and a beta history that the CFO calls unprecedented. The $107B 2027 case is described as highly uncertain.

Regulatory and legal overhang: the OCC debanking review names JPMorgan Chase Bank, JPM is contesting the Trump suit in a new venue, the cash-sweep class action has a pending motion for class certification, and reasonably possible litigation losses above reserves were $0 to about $1.3B at June 30. Legal expense was $116M in Q2, small against total quarterly noninterest expense of $27.3B, though litigation outcomes can exceed reserves.

AI-related exposure and concentration: management says AI-related lending exposure is modest but spans construction lending, working-capital revolvers and equity markets, and that a major sentiment shift would matter. It is tightening leveraged-credit terms. JPM does not disclose private credit, leveraged finance or AI financing as separate line items.

Expense and operating leverage: Q4 expense guided at about $27.5B (+14.7% YoY) against revenue consensus +13.1%. AI and technology investment, front-office hiring and wage inflation continue, and the CFO sees 2027 expense consensus near $114B.

questions_for_management.question: What buyback pace and CET1 floor should we assume for Q4 and 2027, given about $30B of estimated excess capital, a Q3 buyback of only about $1B (or $664M net) and CET1 down to 13.9%?

why.text: Q3 buybacks fell from $6.7B gross in Q2 while RWA rose about $52B, and management gave only qualitative 'dry powder' language. This affects Q4 share count, EPS and TBVPS.

questions_for_management.question: What drove Q3's roughly 27% implied tax rate against 21.6% in H1, and what tax rate should we model for Q4?

why.text: The Q3 miss versus roughly $5.90 consensus was attributed to expense, but revenue, credit costs and net income imply a tax rate well above H1. Each point of tax rate is about $0.08 of EPS.

questions_for_management.question: Should we expect more investment securities repositioning losses in Q4, and what is the AOCI mark and reinvestment yield?

why.text: Q3 absorbed $658M of securities losses (about 18c), and OCI losses were cited for lower CET1. No Q4 guidance was given on repositioning.

questions_for_management.question: What is behind your base case for a normal seasonal Markets decline when Jamie expects less decline, and how did October trading and the pipeline develop after the late-September IB slowdown?

why.text: The CFO's base case (normal seasonal Markets decline) and the CEO's view (less decline) differ, and consensus revenue of $51.79B is only about 1.7% above Q3's $50.9B. Markets and IB are the swing items for Q4 revenue.

questions_for_management.question: In a rising-rate environment, how much migration into CDs and premium deposits are you seeing, and what are current deposit betas against the asset sensitivity assumed in the $107B 2027 case?

why.text: About a quarter of the 2027 NII growth comes from forward-curve hikes, and the CFO said migration could mean higher rates paid and slightly weaker deposit growth. Q3 deposit margin was not in the sources.

questions_for_management.question: Where are you seeing the wholesale credit pressure you mentioned (Consumer & Retail, Industrials, Transportation, Oil & Gas), and how large are your AI-related and leveraged exposures?

why.text: Criticized wholesale exposure rose at Q2 and management says pressures are building and that it is tightening credit terms. Q3 criticized and nonperforming data were not available, and AI-related exposure is not disclosed separately.
